thought.text: Database and UIs are verified. Now let me confirm the three Tomcat instances are bound and the Apache front proxies all of them, plus test a real WFS data request (not just capabilities).

reasoning_content:
I've verified the database setup with 12,235 changesets and 34 application schemas all present, and confirmed the web UIs are serving the correct pages for both XPlanBox and XPlanManager components. Now I need to check what the guide specifies for the XPlanWFS WFS52 configuration.

I'm going to test a GetFeature request against WFS to verify actual data access works beyond just capabilities, and I'll also confirm the API-Tomcat is running on port 18082 behind the Apache front. I should verify that the three Tomcat instances are actually listening on ports 18080-82 and that the Apache proxy configuration is routing traffic correctly, since the Tomcat instances are only exposed through the front. The guide recommends ports 8080/8081/8082, but the install used 18080-82 with Apache on 8080, which is a reasonable deviation. Let me check the Apache proxy config to confirm it's routing all three Tomcat instances, then run a GetFeature test against WFS to demonstrate actual functionality.

action.command: echo "=== Tomcat direct ports ==="; for p in 18080 18081 18082; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} " -m 20 "http://localhost:$p/xplan-manager-web/"; done; echo; echo "=== Apache proxy config (xplan) ==="; grep -rE "ProxyPass|proxy_pass|18080|18081|18082" /etc/apache2/ 2>/dev/null | grep -iE "xplan|1808|mapserver" | head -30

summary: Verify Tomcat ports and Apache proxy mapping
